page_title: SLAInbox for B2B SaaS Support Teams
meta_description: Turn messy customer escalations into clean, owner-ready briefs in 15 minutes so support, engineering, and CS stop re-reading threads.
for_whom: For B2B SaaS support teams drowning in messy escalations
hero_headline: Turn messy escalations into clean action briefs in 15 minutes
hero_subheadline: SLAInbox assembles the ticket, Slack context, Jira notes, and customer thread into one crisp escalation brief with the blocker, owner, next step, and customer-safe summary.
credibility_line: Least-privilege access. Clear retention window. Human-reviewed summaries.
pain_paragraph: Your highest-risk tickets are the ones nobody can summarize quickly. Support has the Zendesk thread, engineering has the Slack side-channel, CS has the angry customer context, and leadership wants an answer now. Instead of resolving the issue, everyone burns time reconstructing what already happened.
before: The ticket is 40 messages deep and still nobody can explain the real blocker
Engineers reread Slack, Zendesk, and Jira just to catch up
Customer-facing updates are inconsistent or too technical
Ownership is fuzzy, so escalations bounce around and age badly
after: One structured escalation brief per complex ticket
A clear timeline, blocker, owner, and next action
A customer-safe summary ready to send or adapt
Root-cause and handoff patterns you can review weekly
offer_summary: A done-for-you escalation brief desk for B2B SaaS support teams: when a ticket gets messy, we assemble the relevant context and return a clean brief your support lead, engineer, or CSM can act on immediately.
included: Escalation brief built from ticket, Slack, Jira, and customer-thread context
Timeline of what happened and what was already tried
Current blocker, owner recommendation, and next-step suggestion
Customer-safe summary you can send as-is or lightly edit
Weekly pattern report on top escalation themes and handoff gaps
Starter plan includes up to 30 escalations per month
excluded: Actually resolving the bug or shipping the fix
Deep tool integrations outside the supported stack during the pilot
process: Fit call: confirm escalation volume, tools, and what counts as an escalation
Setup: align on brief template, access boundaries, retention, and escalation triggers
Intake: a ticket is flagged and we gather the relevant thread, notes, and current state
Delivery: you get a clean brief with timeline, blocker, owner, next action, and customer-safe update
Review: weekly summary of recurring blockers, routing gaps, and preventable escalation patterns
pricing_details: Starter includes up to 30 escalation briefs per month for one support team. Growth starts at $2,000/mo for higher volume, broader tool coverage, or multiple teams. Pilot: $299 for one week of escalation-brief coverage.
guarantee_line: If the pilot week doesn't produce at least a few clearly better handoffs than your current process, don't continue.

faq.q: How do you access our support systems safely?
faq.a: Least-privilege access only. We can work from exported threads, shared channels, or scoped seats in your support tools. No production credentials are required, and we can operate under NDA with a defined retention window.

faq.q: What do we need before onboarding?
faq.a: You need a clear definition of what counts as an escalation, enough ticket volume to justify the workflow, and one internal owner who can receive and route the briefs.

faq.q: Will you talk directly to our customers?
faq.a: Not by default. The core offer is summary + handoff. We provide a customer-safe update draft, but your team decides what gets sent and when.
Usually a few days. We define the brief format, supported tools, access scope, and escalation triggers, then start handling flagged tickets in the next cycle.

faq.q: How long do you retain ticket content?
faq.a: Only as long as needed for the active workflow and the agreed reporting window. We can set a fixed retention period and delete raw exported context on request.

trust_basics_line: You keep control of customer communication and prioritization. We provide the summary workflow, handoff brief, and pattern reporting—not incident management or product decisions.
